speaker: Unknown
en: We've all spent money on something that seemed incredible but didn't live up to the hype.
zh: 我们都曾把钱花在那些看起来不可思议但最终名不副实的东西上。

speaker: Unknown
en: A kitchen gadget, a car.
zh: 一个厨房小工具，一辆车。

speaker: Unknown
en: When it doesn't deliver, the disappointment is real.
zh: 当它没能兑现承诺时，失望是真实的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Marketers suffer from this too, chasing metrics that look great but don't translate into revenue.
zh: 营销人员也深受其苦，追逐那些看起来漂亮但不能转化为收入的指标。

speaker: Unknown
en: LinkedIn calls that bull spend.
zh: LinkedIn 把这称为 bull spend(无谓开销)。

speaker: Unknown
en: Invest in what matters and reach the right buyers with LinkedIn ads.
zh: 投资于真正重要的东西，用 LinkedIn 广告触达正确的买家。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can target by company, industry, job title, and more.
zh: 你可以按公司、行业、职位头衔等进行定向投放。

speaker: Unknown
en: LinkedIn ads also generates the highest ROAS of all major ad networks.
zh: LinkedIn 广告还是所有主要广告网络中 ROAS(广告支出回报率)最高的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Spend $250 on your first campaign on LinkedIn ads and get a $250 credit for the next one.
zh: 在 LinkedIn 广告上为你的第一波广告活动花 250 美元，就能获得下一次广告活动的 250 美元抵用额度。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just go to linkedin.com slash scale.
zh: 只需访问 linkedin.com/scale。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's linkedin.com slash scale.
zh: 也就是 linkedin.com/scale。

speaker: Unknown
en: Terms and conditions apply.
zh: 适用条款和条件。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI is full of possibilities.
zh: AI 充满了可能性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Enterprises run on realities.
zh: 而企业运转靠的是现实。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's why PEGA combines the world's most powerful AI with the governance, transparency, and control enterprises demand.
zh: 这就是为什么 PEGA 将世界上最强大的 AI 与企业所要求的治理、透明度和控制相结合。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can move faster, adapt faster, and scale AI with confidence.
zh: 这样你就能更快地行动、更快地适应，并充满信心地扩展 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: All the power of AI, none of the uncertainty.
zh: 拥有 AI 的全部力量，没有不确定性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Learn more at PEGA.com slash AI.
zh: 了解更多信息请访问 PEGA.com/AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a privilege to be working on these things at this moment in time.
zh: 能在这个时刻做这些事情是一种荣幸。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's something that we all feel like a sort of like a deep collective responsibility.
zh: 我们所有人都感到这像是一种深层的集体责任。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's this deep sense of, you know, hey, you know, it's like, we really must get this right.
zh: 所以有一种很深的感觉，你知道，就是，嘿，我们真的必须把这件事做对。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, this is the time to just put in the effort so that, you know, this technology ends up putting humans and humanity at the center of it and not humans being an afterthought, you know, because relentlessly just pursuing, you know, whatever, like automation, it's just like, that's not why we're here.
zh: 而且，你知道，现在正是投入努力的时候，这样，你知道，这项技术最终会把人类和人性置于中心，而不是让人类成为事后才想起的东西，因为一味地追求，你知道，不管什么，比如自动化，那不是我们在这里的原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, that's not why I'm here.
zh: 而且，你知道，这也不是我在这里的原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want this to just like benefit all, you know, benefit humanity.
zh: 我希望它能惠及所有人，你知道，造福人类。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there is this like incredible mission behind it, which is super motivating.
zh: 所以此事背后有一种难以置信的使命感，这非常鼓舞人心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thibaut Sotio leads product at OpenAI.
zh: Thibaut Sotio 在 OpenAI 负责产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: He joined the company two years ago and led the team building Codex, the coding agent, and now oversees OpenAI's core products like ChatGPT.
zh: 他两年前加入公司，领导了构建编程智能体 Codex 的团队，现在负责 OpenAI 的核心产品，比如 ChatGPT。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today, I'm sitting down with Thibaut to talk about OpenAI's newest releases, what it's like to work inside a frontier lab during this extraordinary moment, and his approach to safety, trust, and alignment.
zh: 今天，我与 Thibaut 坐下来，聊聊 OpenAI 最新的发布、在这个非凡时刻在一家前沿实验室内部工作是什么感觉，以及他在安全、信任和对齐方面的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm Rana El-Khalyubi, and this is Pioneers of AI, a podcast taking you behind the scenes of the AI revolution.
zh: 我是 Rana El-Khalyubi，这里是 Pioneers of AI，一档带你了解 AI 革命幕后故事的播客。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hi, Thibaut.
zh: 你好，Thibaut。

speaker: Unknown
en: Welcome to Pioneers of AI.
zh: 欢迎来到 Pioneers of AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm so excited for our conversation.
zh: 我对我们的对话感到非常兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks for having me.
zh: 谢谢邀请我。

speaker: Unknown
en: All right.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you lead the product team at OpenAI.
zh: 你在 OpenAI 领导产品团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: Help us understand the scope of your role.
zh: 帮我们理解一下你职责的范围。

speaker: Unknown
en: How big is your team?
zh: 你的团队有多大？

speaker: Unknown
en: All that.
zh: 诸如此类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The biggest part is ChatGPT that everyone knows about.
zh: 最主要的部分是大家都熟知的 ChatGPT。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we also have specialist things such as Codex, which is for coders and technical people out there.
zh: 然后我们还有一些专门的产品，比如面向程序员和技术人员的 Codex。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then there's also a whole part around our API and our platform to support building a whole bunch of products out there when they rely on our models.
zh: 然后还有围绕我们 API 和平台的整整一部分，用于支持当外面的众多产品依赖我们的模型时进行构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so all together, that's the majority of the products we have here at OpenAI.
zh: 这些加在一起，就是我们在这里 OpenAI 拥有的产品的大多数。

speaker: Unknown
en: Am I right in understanding that basically the researchers at OpenAI are building the models and then at some point they hand off this model to you and you productize it?
zh: 我这样理解对吗：基本上 OpenAI 的研究人员负责构建模型，然后在某个时候他们把这个模型交给你，由你把它产品化？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that a right way to think about it?
zh: 这样思考是对的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Almost.
zh: 差不多。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we collaborate quite early on, on the next...
zh: 所以我们很早就开始协作，关于下一……

speaker: Unknown
en: type of capabilities that we want to have in the model.
zh: 我们想让模型拥有的能力类型。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for example, say that we want our models to be able to handle secure payments.
zh: 比如说，假如我们想让我们的模型能够处理安全支付。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then we would go and work with researchers specifically on these kinds of capabilities, figure out the right kind of data we need to craft for it.
zh: 那么我们就会专门和研究人员一起研究这类能力，弄清楚我们需要为此打造什么样的数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: The right kind of evaluations we need for it and then how to bring it into a product.
zh: 我们需要什么样的评估，然后如何把它带进产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the collaboration starts quite early on.
zh: 所以合作很早就开始了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then we train the model and then the researchers hand it over and then we serve it and then we package it into the product.
zh: 然后我们训练模型，研究人员把它交给我们，我们进行服务，再把它打包进产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: Very cool.
zh: 非常酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, so we are talking at the start of October.
zh: 好，我们是在十月初进行这次对话的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Dev Day just happened.
zh: Dev Day 刚刚结束。

speaker: Unknown
en: For those who are not familiar with Dev Day, give us a sense of what it's like.
zh: 给那些不了解 Dev Day 的听众讲讲，它是什么样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Dev Day is the day that we like to spend with the developer community out there.
zh: Dev Day 是我们喜欢与外面的开发者社区共度的一天。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are like, I think, 2,500 people in person, and then we also stream it live.
zh: 我记得大概有 2500 人到场，另外我们还做了直播。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we talk about a lot of things.
zh: 我们聊很多话题。

speaker: Unknown
en: That, you know, we're excited about new products, new models, new ways, you know, for developers and product startups and enterprises to build out there on top of our platform.
zh: 你知道的，我们为新产品、新模型、新的方式感到兴奋，让开发者、产品初创公司和企业能在我们的平台上进行构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, yeah, this week was super, super energizing to also spend time, you know, with people in person.
zh: 所以，是的，这一周能和大家当面交流，真是超级、超级令人振奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm always quite humbled when I talk to folks like, you know, they flew in from Brazil, they flew in from Asia, they flew in from Europe just to spend time with us.
zh: 我每次和大家聊天时总是很感动，你知道，他们从巴西飞过来，从亚洲飞过来，从欧洲飞过来，就为了和我们共度时光。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's a real privilege.
zh: 我觉得这真是一种荣幸。

speaker: Unknown
en: Take us behind the scenes.
zh: 带我们看看幕后吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, what is it like the day before?
zh: 比如前一天是什么样的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you pulling all-nighters?
zh: 你们会通宵吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: The team works very hard, for sure, for sure.
zh: 团队肯定非常努力，肯定的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It always comes together quite, quite, quite, you know, last minute.
zh: 事情总是在最后关头才凑齐，真的是最后关头。

speaker: Unknown
en: Three days before, the keynote comes together, the events come together, the presentations come together.
zh: 前三天，主题演讲才成型，活动才成型，演示才成型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, because if you start planning six months ago, it's like way outdated by the time you announced, right?
zh: 是啊，因为如果你六个月前就开始规划，到发布的时候早就过时了，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's right.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, we're moving so fast these days.
zh: 我是说，我们这些日子节奏非常快。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, we're able to build faster than ever before.
zh: 你知道的，我们的构建速度比以往任何时候都快。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're able to stay, you know, much closer to the community and just really listen to that feedback.
zh: 我们能更贴近社区，真正倾听反馈。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is like the part of the job I love the most is, you know, we can try something new and then get a whole host of feedback and then, you know, ship a much better version the next day.
zh: 这是我最喜欢这份工作的部分，就是我们可以尝试新东西，然后收到一大堆反馈，然后第二天就能发布一个更好的版本。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you're really building with that community.
zh: 所以你真的是在和那个社区一起构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: I find the community that we have at DevDay is super awesome and super forgiving in that sense.
zh: 我觉得我们在 DevDay 拥有的社区非常棒，而且在这个意义上非常宽容。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm also chronically online, so it's just kind of fun to finally see people in person.
zh: 而且我长期泡在网上，所以终于能当面见到大家还是挺有趣的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you take a beat after Dev Day?
zh: Dev Day 之后你会停一下吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you and the team, like, take a day off to celebrate or unwind or not really?
zh: 你和团队会不会休一天假来庆祝或者放松，还是不会？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, a lot of people are off today.
zh: 是的，今天很多人放假。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some folks are off next week.
zh: 有些人下周休假。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, it's all about modulating your energy, but also OpenAI is like such a fascinating and high energy place that, you know, it can at times, like, you know, be hard to disconnect just because, you know, there's so much, you know, good stuff happening.
zh: 你知道的，关键在于调节自己的精力，但 OpenAI 也是一个非常迷人、充满高能量的地方，有时候会很难完全抽离，因为有太多好的事情在发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: Next week, I am forcing part of the team to just like take time off.
zh: 下周，我会强迫团队的一部分人去休假。

speaker: Unknown
en: Forcing, okay, keyword here.
zh: 强迫，好的，关键词来了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I'm just like, no, you have to leave your laptop at work, yeah.
zh: 对，我就是那种——不，你必须把笔记本电脑留在公司，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, so you launched Dots at the event, which is very exciting, and it's basically a new suite of agents that help you get stuff done.
zh: 好，所以你们在活动上发布了 Dots，这非常令人兴奋，它基本上是一套新的智能体，帮你把事情办成。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are your favorite examples of how people are using Dots?
zh: 你最喜欢的人们使用 Dots 的例子有哪些？

speaker: Unknown
en: My favorite example was...
zh: 我最喜欢的例子是……

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, maybe my own dot during the keynote where just like five minutes before we had a failure during the live demo, like my dot messaged me and was like, hey, by the way, like production is down.
zh: 你知道的，可能是主题演讲期间我自己的 dot，就在现场演示出故障前五分钟，我的 dot 给我发消息说，嘿，顺便说一下，生产环境挂了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh my God, okay.
zh: 天哪，好吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Rob Lee should care about this because, you know, you have like the live demo, like, you know, I looked at the script and, you know, this is going to interfere with the demo.
zh: Rob Lee 应该关心这个，因为你知道，现场演示，你看，我看了脚本，这会干扰演示。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, do you want me to kind of have a look at fixing it?
zh: 然后，你想让我看看怎么修它吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, if it cannot do something about it itself, like, you know, maybe I can.
zh: 然后，如果它自己没办法处理，你知道，也许我可以。

speaker: Unknown
en: Unfortunately, we were not able to fix it, you know, just in the nick of time.
zh: 不幸的是，我们没能在最后关头把它修好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, you know, we reposted another shot of the demo online just yesterday, which was super appreciated again by the community.
zh: 然后就在昨天，我们把另一次演示的录像发到了网上，再次受到社区的大力赞赏。

speaker: Unknown
en: But like that's the kind of example where, you know, it's just over time because you interact with it, it learns your preferences and what's important to you and then can help you in the right way in a way that's like super seamless and, you know, just really in the context.
zh: 但这就是那种例子，你知道，随着时间的推移，因为你和它互动，它会了解你的偏好和什么对你重要，然后能以非常无缝的方式、真正贴合上下文的方式，用正确的方式帮助你。

speaker: Unknown
en: The biggest magic is the fact that I don't have to check everything else anymore.
zh: 最大的魔力在于我不再需要去检查其他所有东西了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't have to check like my emails or my Slack or like, you know, all the messages.
zh: 我不用再去看我的邮件、我的 Slack，或者你知道的，所有那些消息。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I can just kind of trust that.
zh: 而我可以就这样信任它。

speaker: Unknown
en: If it didn't bring something up, it's like, you know, probably not important.
zh: 如果它没提出什么，那就说明，你知道，大概率不重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I just can go about my day, you know, in a very peaceful and zen way.
zh: 所以我就可以继续过我的日子，你知道，以一种非常平静、禅意的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think trust is a keyword here and I'll share a personal example.
zh: 我认为信任是这里的关键词，我来分享一个个人的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I use ChatGPT Finance and I love it.
zh: 我在用 ChatGPT Finance,我很喜欢它。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like connected to all my bank accounts.
zh: 它连接了我所有的银行账户。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I was sharing that with my 23 year old daughter who's not really into a lot of AI.
zh: 但我和我 23 岁的女儿分享这件事时，她对 AI 不太感兴趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: And she was like, really?
zh: 她就说，真的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: You gave OpenAI access to all your bank accounts?
zh: 你把所有银行账户的访问权限都给了 OpenAI?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, are you crazy?
zh: 你是不是疯了？

speaker: Unknown
en: So how do you build trust with consumers so that they do feel comfortable and confident that they can share this type of information with OpenAI and also trust to give it agency to act on your behalf?
zh: 那么，你如何与消费者建立信任，让他们感到安心和有信心，愿意把这类信息分享给 OpenAI,并且信任地赋予它代表你行事的能动性(agency)?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think this is a big one.
zh: 我认为这是个很大的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't recommend like, you know, giving access to everything like, you know, right off the bat, you know, you start with limited access, you can set, you know, your own guardrails and like by default, it's like very, very cautious and will ask you literally for approval for everything.
zh: 我不建议，你知道，一开始就把所有权限都交出去，你知道，你从有限的访问权限开始，你可以设置自己的护栏，而且默认情况下，它是非常非常谨慎的，基本上每一件事都会请求你的批准。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, it's just, I feel comfortable, you know, you acting on my behalf in this scenario, I feel comfortable, you know, you're going and drafting an email, you know, but like never send it.
zh: 你知道的，在这个场景下我放心让你代表我行事，我放心让你去起草一封邮件，但是绝对不要发送。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're always in control.
zh: 你始终在掌控之中。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is super important because I think the utility that you get from these systems is kind of capped by how much access it has.
zh: 这一点超级重要，因为我认为你从这些系统中获得的效用，在某种程度上受限于它拥有多少访问权限。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you don't want your personal intelligence to kind of be boxed up and have access to nothing.
zh: 而你不会希望你的个人智能被框起来，什么权限都没有。

speaker: Unknown
en: Otherwise, it would not be very useful in your life.
zh: 否则，它在你的生活中就不会很有用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's up to us to kind of earn that trust and earn the right to provide that utility to you.
zh: 所以要靠我们来赢得那种信任，赢得为你提供那种效用的权利。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we take it obviously super, super seriously.
zh: 我们显然对此非常非常认真。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to talk about Astra, about the Astra model for a bit.
zh: 我想谈谈 Astra,谈谈 Astra 模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: You actually called the lead up to this DevDay your most ambitious sprint yet.
zh: 你曾说这次 DevDay 之前的冲刺是你迄今最有雄心的冲刺。

speaker: Unknown
en: Give us an example of what Astra made possible that wasn't possible before.
zh: 给我们举个例子，说明 Astra 让哪些以前不可能的事情成为可能。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's right.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: So a clear example is that we had, you know, previous to DevDay, like roughly a month ago, we had a separate code base for ChatGPT.com on web.
zh: 一个很明显的例子是，在 DevDay 之前，大概一个月前，我们在网页端的 ChatGPT.com 有一个单独的代码库。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we decided to merge the desktop application and ChatGPT.com.
zh: 所以我们决定把桌面应用和 ChatGPT.com 合并。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is something that would have traditionally taken at least six, maybe 12 months, and something that you would do very, very carefully.
zh: 这在传统上至少需要六个月，也许十二个月，而且是需要非常非常小心去做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because this is our main surface.
zh: 因为这是我们的主入口。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have, like, you know, hundreds of millions of users visiting this website, right?
zh: 我们有，你知道，数亿用户访问这个网站，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we just merged it, and we merged it in 30 days.
zh: 而我们直接合并了它，而且在 30 天内完成了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have to ask you this question.
zh: 我必须问你这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who wrote most of the code?
zh: 大部分代码是谁写的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Was it AI or humans or both?
zh: 是 AI、人类，还是两者都有？

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you tell us?
zh: 能告诉我们吗？
